data.description:
# LLM gate runs record no per-run request or tool-call counts, so the gates cannot be tuned

## The gap

**Nothing durably records how many model requests or tool calls a gate run consumed.** There is no
usage log on disk, and the audit sidecar carries criteria and citations but no request/tool-call
counts. Established while investigating [rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e]: the control-group question
"how many of the 240 available requests did the epics that closed cleanly actually use?" **could not
be answered from the store at all.**

## Why this matters — it is why the same bug recurred six times

The completion gate's step budget has been raised **five times** across its history
([rebar:c827-2a23-cd00-473e]'s history sweep), a hard tool-call cap was proposed and deferred
([rebar:7c58-...]) then proposed and rejected ([rebar:b2bb-...]), and the verifier's own creating
epic was force-closed citing the limitation as "documented". **Every one of those decisions was made
without spend data**, because the data was never recorded.

The cost of that absence is measurable: answering a single question about this gate required **four
live instrumented runs at ~20-50 minutes each**, re-deriving numbers that should have been a query.
And the tuning advice the docs give (`docs/llm-framework.md:698-704` — "a high recursion limit means
you're paying for a loop, fix the loop") is unactionable, because nothing tells an operator whether
they are paying for a loop or for breadth.

This is the same **"computed then discarded"** shape as two sibling defects: the repetition
diagnostic that `interpret_failure` builds and `raise_completion_workflow_failure` drops
([rebar:c827-...]), and the deterministic child-closure proof collapsed to a boolean
([rebar:6ec8-24c7-182b-40d0]). The value is produced and thrown away one frame from the surface.

## Scope note

`usage_log` machinery already exists in-tree (e.g. `usage_log.failure_usage`,
`usage_log.capture_attempt_messages`), and `run_ctx.usage` is live inside the tool-filter predicate.
**Establish what is already captured before adding anything** — the likely defect is that the data is
captured and not persisted, in which case this is a wiring job, not new accounting. Do not build a
second, parallel usage mechanism.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] every LLM gate run persists, durably and queryably: model requests consumed, tool calls
      consumed, the applicable limits, the step name, the ticket id, and wall-clock duration
- [ ] the FAILURE path records it too — a run that exhausts its budget or errors is exactly when the
      numbers are needed, and is the case most likely to be missed
- [ ] enough signal is recorded to distinguish a LOOP from genuine BREADTH after the fact without
      re-running: at minimum the distinct-vs-total tool-call-signature counts, so the windowed
      distinct-ratio [rebar:70bc-ab05-6d4c-45a0] establishes can be computed from the record
- [ ] the record is reachable by an operator without instrumenting a run — state the exact command or
      path that retrieves it, and prove it by retrieving one
- [ ] a test pins that the counts are actually WRITTEN on both the success and the exhaustion paths,
      with a fixture that varies which path is taken (a success-only fixture would be vacuous here)
- [ ] no second parallel usage mechanism is introduced where the existing one can be wired

## Testing

    pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 4 --dist worksteal -q
    make lint && make typecheck
    # then retrieve a real recorded run and show the counts
data.title: LLM gate runs record no per-run request or tool-call counts, so the gates cannot be tuned
